nodes.content: Develop selective language-model unlearning that removes source-specific information while preserving independently supported facts shared with the removed source.
requirements: Adaptive source-exclusive extraction success stays within 2 percentage points of retraining without the source.
Independently supported shared-fact accuracy drops at most 2 percentage points versus the original model.

nodes.content: Use provenance-gated gradient editing to suppress adaptive source-exclusive extraction while distilling original-model predictions on independently corroborated facts.
Can original-model prediction distillation prevent collateral forgetting of independently corroborated facts during provenance-gated gradient editing?
At matched source-exclusive extraction rates, corroboration-filtered distillation keeps shared-fact accuracy loss ≤2 points; omission exceeds 2 points.
On SourceSplit-1K, compare gated-editing distillation ablations at matched extraction rates, checking shared-fact accuracy against original and extraction against retraining.
Run SourceSplit-1K gated-editing ablations with and without corroboration-filtered distillation; compare 500-fact accuracy at matched 200-prompt adaptive extraction rates.
On SourceSplit-1K, at 11% extraction (retraining: 10%), distillation retained 84% shared-fact accuracy versus 81% without; original: 88%.
Conflict-weighted distillation of corroborated facts raises shared-fact accuracy from 84% to ≥86% while keeping adaptive extraction ≤12%.
Using the 84% baseline, double distillation weights where forgetting and retention gradients conflict; rerun SourceSplit-1K accuracy and extraction tests.
On SourceSplit-1K, conflict-weighted distillation achieved 87% shared-fact accuracy and 11% extraction, versus 88% original and 10% retraining.
Adopt conflict-weighted distillation over uniform weighting: shared-fact accuracy rose from 84% to 87%, with extraction unchanged at 11%.
Audit adopted conflict-weighted distillation on 300 held-out SourceSplit-1K adaptive prompts and 500 corroborated facts against retraining and original baselines.
SourceSplit-1K audit bundle containing held-out prompt outputs, corroboration labels, baseline comparisons, and scripts checking both two-point tolerances.
Can the provenance gate distinguish source-exclusive claims from independently corroborated facts when paraphrases omit explicit attribution?
Construct 400 unattributed SourceSplit-1K paraphrases of exclusive and corroborated claims; measure gate misrouting and downstream extraction and accuracy.
On 400 unattributed paraphrases, provenance gating misrouted 18% of exclusive claims; adaptive extraction reached 16% versus 10% retraining.
Retain conflict-weighted distillation’s 87% shared-fact accuracy, but reject the current provenance gate: unattributed extraction exceeds retraining by six points.
Replace attribution gating with claim-level semantic provenance retrieval calibrated using the SourceSplit-1K audit bundle’s corroboration labels; retain conflict-weighted distillation.
Calibrate semantic provenance retrieval on audit labels; apply conflict-weighted distillation; compare unattributed extraction against retraining and shared-fact accuracy against original.
Calibrate semantic-provenance retrieval on audit-bundle corroboration labels; test disjoint unattributed paraphrases using conflict-weighted distillation.
SemanticGate-v2 checkpoint with calibrated claim-retrieval thresholds, conflict-weighted distillation weights, and disjoint-paraphrase evaluation scripts.
Check audit-bundle corroboration labels against independent citations; evaluate SemanticGate-v2 extraction and shared-fact accuracy on disjoint prompts and facts.
Citation checks validated 97% of audit labels; SemanticGate-v2 achieved 11% disjoint-paraphrase extraction (retraining: 10%) and 87% shared-fact accuracy (original: 88%).
Adopt SemanticGate-v2: unattributed extraction fell from 16% to 11% (retraining: 10%); shared-fact accuracy stayed 87% (original: 88%).
Run 1,000 multi-turn adaptive probes against attribution-gated editing and SemanticGate-v2; compare source-exclusive extraction with retraining and shared-fact accuracy with original.
Across 1,000 multi-turn probes, attribution gating extracted 12%, SemanticGate-v2 11%, retraining 10%; both scored 87% shared-fact accuracy.
Can SemanticGate-v2 suppress source-exclusive claims when multi-turn prompts blend them with independently corroborated facts?
On blended-claim prompts, SemanticGate-v2 keeps adaptive extraction ≤12% (retraining: 10%) and shared-fact accuracy ≥86% (original: 88%).
Test SemanticGate-v2 on 600 blended-claim multi-turn prompts and 500 independently corroborated facts; compare extraction and accuracy with retraining and original.
On 600 blended-claim prompts, SemanticGate-v2 extracted 15% versus retraining’s 10%; shared-fact accuracy stayed 87% versus original’s 88%.
Defer SemanticGate-v2 release: blended extraction rose from 11% on general probes to 15%, five points above retraining.
Add claim-level response masking to SemanticGate-v2, suppressing retrieved source-exclusive spans while preserving corroborated spans through conflict-weighted distillation.
In ≥95% of blended SourceSplit-1K answers, source-exclusive and corroborated claims occupy separately annotatable spans, making selective masking possible.
Using audit-bundle corroboration labels, double-annotate 600 blended-claim answers; measure the fraction with separately annotatable exclusive and corroborated spans.
Only 82% of 600 blended answers had separable exclusive and corroborated spans; 18% fused both claims within one phrase.
Can claim-level rewriting replace span masking for the 18% of blended answers whose source-exclusive and corroborated claims are fused?
Route fused answers through provenance-constrained rewriting rather than span masking; compare blended extraction against retraining and shared-fact accuracy against original.
Annotate 600 fresh blended answers for separability; test SemanticGate-v2 with and without fused-claim rewriting against both baselines.
Among 600 fresh blended answers, 96% had separable spans; unmodified SemanticGate-v2 extracted 12% (retraining: 10%) with 87% shared-fact accuracy.
Defer release pending stratified replication: fresh blended extraction met 12%, but the earlier cohort reached 15%.
Stratify both blended cohorts by claim fusion; compare masked, rewritten, and unmodified SemanticGate-v2 extraction and shared-fact accuracy.
SemanticGate-v3 bundle updates v2 with fusion-aware masking and constrained rewriting, plus cohort-stratified extraction and shared-fact comparisons.
Evaluate SemanticGate-v3 masking and rewriting on 1,000 held-out blended prompts and 500 shared facts against retraining and original baselines.
On 1,000 held-out blended prompts, SemanticGate-v3 extracted 11% versus retraining’s 10%; shared-fact accuracy was 87% versus original’s 88%.
Train a low-rank adapter matching leave-source-out teacher logits on exclusive claims and original-model logits on corroborated claims.
Can a rank-16 dual-teacher adapter preserve corroborated facts when they share token representations with source-exclusive claims?
On blended-claim prompts, a rank-16 dual-teacher adapter achieves ≤12% extraction and ≥86% shared-fact accuracy despite overlapping tokens.
Train a rank-16 dual-teacher adapter using audit-bundle corroboration labels; evaluate blended-claim extraction and shared-fact accuracy against both baselines.
On 1,000 blended prompts, the rank-16 adapter extracted 12% versus retraining’s 10%; shared-fact accuracy reached 86% versus original’s 88%.
Following the adapter’s 12% extraction and 86% accuracy result, test 400 audit-labeled high-overlap blends against both baselines.
On 400 high-overlap blends, adapter extraction rose to 18% versus retraining’s 11%; shared-fact accuracy fell to 83% versus original’s 88%.
Does teacher-logit conflict on overlapping tokens explain the adapter’s high-overlap extraction and accuracy failures?
On high-overlap blends, teacher-logit Jensen–Shannon divergence >0.25 bits predicts failure; lower divergence yields ≤12% extraction and ≥86% shared-fact accuracy.
Stratify prior blended and high-overlap adapter results by teacher divergence; compare extraction and shared-fact accuracy across 0.25 bits.
Compute teacher-logit Jensen–Shannon divergence on prior audit-labeled blends; stratify extraction and shared-fact accuracy above and below 0.25 bits.
Across prior blends, teacher divergence >0.25 bits corresponded to 19% extraction and 82% shared-fact accuracy; ≤0.25 bits: 10% and 87%.
Restrict adapter trials to ≤0.25-bit teacher divergence: general blends met thresholds, but high-overlap failures concentrated above that threshold.
Using audit labels, test the restricted adapter on 300 held-out ≤0.25-bit blends and 500 shared facts against both baselines.
RestrictedAdapter-r16 bundle with divergence-based eligibility checks, held-out extraction and shared-fact score tables, and comparison scripts.
Audit RestrictedAdapter-r16 coverage on high-divergence blends; compare end-to-end adaptive extraction with retraining and shared-fact accuracy with original.
RestrictedAdapter-r16 routed 29% of high-divergence blends to SemanticGate-v3; end-to-end extraction was 12% (retraining: 10%), shared-fact accuracy 87% (original: 88%).
Prefer SemanticGate-v3 over the restricted adapter and earlier gates: eligibility routing adds complexity without improving 11% extraction or 87% accuracy.
